message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"5.26","text":"For our mind, whenever at the outset it takes an impression of the beloved woman’s appearance under the influence of pleasure, is tormented through memory, as though always gazing at her form in a mirror; and when it does not attain its desire, it devises the paths to attainment, but when it does attain it, it grows still more, like a fire amply supplied with fuel, and especially when fear has not already been impressed on the lover’s soul before the passion. For just as water extinguishes fire, so fear too is an extinguisher of irrational desire. Therefore, since I learned from a certain Jew both to think and to do what befits God, I am not made easy prey to adultery by false myths. But may God help you, as you wish and strive to be self-controlled while your soul is inflamed with erotic passion, and may he provide the cure.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ εἶδος τῆς ἐρωμένης ἀπομάξηται","chosen":"takes an impression of the beloved woman’s appearance","rationale":"ἀπομάσσομαι can describe taking or receiving an impression, fitting the following mirror image; “copies” or “imprints upon itself” are also possible."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιτυχὼν δὲ μᾶλλον αὔξεται","chosen":"but when it does attain it, it grows still more","rationale":"The English pronouns preserve the referential tension: νοῦς is the formal subject, while the context may make the growing element the desire or passion."},{"source_quote":"τὸ πῦρ τῆς ὕλης εὐποροῦν","chosen":"a fire amply supplied with fuel","rationale":"ὕλη can mean material or wood; in the fire image it denotes available fuel."},{"source_quote":"εὐἄλωτος πρὸς μοιχείαν","chosen":"easy prey to adultery","rationale":"εὐάλωτος literally describes what is easily captured, so the rendering preserves the predatory image rather than merely saying “easily persuaded.”"},{"source_quote":"φλεγμαινούσῃ ψυχῇ πρὸς ἔρωτα","chosen":"while your soul is inflamed with erotic passion","rationale":"ἔρως here denotes erotic love or desire, while φλεγμαίνω continues the preceding fire imagery."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"5.27","text":"On hearing the feigned written reply, Appion said, “Do I hate Jews without reason? Now, at any rate, a certain Jew once encountered this woman, brought her over to his religion, and persuaded her to be self-controlled; and from now on it is impossible for her to enter into intimacy with anyone else, because such people, having set God before themselves as the all-seeing observer of actions, steadfastly persist in strict self-control, since they are unable to go unnoticed.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς ὑποκρίτου ἀντιγραφῆς","chosen":"the feigned written reply","rationale":"ἀντιγραφή is a written response, while ὑπόκριτος marks it as assumed, acted, or feigned."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὴν θρησκείαν μεταγαγὼν","chosen":"brought her over to his religion","rationale":"μετάγω expresses transfer to another position, and θρησκεία may denote religion, worship, or religious observance. The possessive is contextually supplied by the preceding Jewish agent, though it is not explicit in Greek."},{"source_quote":"εἰς κοινωνίαν ἑτέρου τινὸς συνελθεῖν","chosen":"to enter into intimacy with anyone else","rationale":"κοινωνία can mean association or participation, but the surrounding discussion of adultery supports sexual intimacy or union here."},{"source_quote":"τὸν θεὸν ὡς παντεπόπτην τῶν πράξεων προθέμενοι","chosen":"having set God before themselves as the all-seeing observer of actions","rationale":"παντεπόπτης presents God as seeing everything; προτίθημι depicts placing that awareness before oneself."},{"source_quote":"ὡς λαθεῖν μὴ δυνάμενοι","chosen":"since they are unable to go unnoticed","rationale":"The infinitive λαθεῖν means escaping notice; the one from whom they cannot remain hidden is implicit from the preceding reference to God."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"5.28","text":"Having heard this, I said to Appion, “Now I will confess the truth to you. I did not fall in love with a woman, nor with any other person, because my soul was entirely expended upon other longings and upon the discovery of true doctrines. And up to the present, after scrutinizing many opinions of philosophers, I inclined toward none of them except only that of the Jews, when a certain merchant of theirs, who sold linen cloths and was staying here in Rome, through a fortunate encounter set before me in simpler terms the belief in one sovereign.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οὐδὲ ἄλλου τινός","chosen":"nor with any other person","rationale":"The genitive form can be masculine, “anyone else,” or neuter, “anything else.” The personal sense fits the statement about falling in love, but the broader alternative remains grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"πάνυ μου τῆς ψυχῆς δεδαπανημένης","chosen":"because my soul was entirely expended","rationale":"δαπανάω conveys spending or consuming resources; here the soul is portrayed as having its energies consumed or devoted elsewhere."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς οὐδένα αὐτῶν ἔνευσα ἢ πρὸς τὸ Ἰουδαίων μόνον","chosen":"I inclined toward none of them except only that of the Jews","rationale":"νεύω literally means nodding or inclining toward something and here denotes assent. The neuter τὸ Ἰουδαίων leaves the Jewish opinion, position, or doctrine implicit."},{"source_quote":"ὀθόνας πιπράσκοντος","chosen":"who sold linen cloths","rationale":"ὀθόνη denotes a linen cloth, sheet, or similar piece of fabric; “linen cloths” retains the commercial object without narrowing its use."},{"source_quote":"τὸ μοναρχικὸν φρόνημα","chosen":"the belief in one sovereign","rationale":"Literally a “monarchic conviction,” the phrase in this theological context concerns sole sovereignty, commonly understood as the sole rule of God; “monotheism” would flatten its wording."},{"source_quote":"ἁπλούστερόν μοι ... παραθεμένου","chosen":"set before me in simpler terms","rationale":"παρατίθημι means placing or presenting something before another, while the comparative ἁπλούστερον can mean “more simply” or, idiomatically, “quite simply.”"}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"5.29","text":"But when Appion heard the truth from me—he who irrationally hates what is Jewish and neither knows nor wishes to know what their belief actually is—he grew angry without examination and, in silence, at once departed from Rome itself. And now, having met him for the first time since then, I reasonably suspect that his anger dates from that time. Nevertheless, in your presence I will ask him what he might have to say about the so-called gods, whose lives—mythologized as subject to every passion—are deliberately sung in public to encourage imitation of such things, and whose tombs are also pointed out in their respective places, in addition to their human passions, as I said.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ Ἰουδαίων","chosen":"what is Jewish","rationale":"The substantivized neuter expression can denote the Jewish position, doctrine, cause, or way; the broad rendering avoids replacing it with the Jewish people themselves."},{"source_quote":"τί ποτε ἐστὶν αὐτῶν τὸ πιστὸν","chosen":"what their belief actually is","rationale":"τὸ πιστόν may denote their belief, faith, or what they hold as trustworthy; the interrogative τί ποτε adds the force of “what exactly” or “actually.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀκρίτως ὀργισθεὶς τῇ σιωπῇ","chosen":"he grew angry without examination and, in silence","rationale":"ἀκρίτως indicates acting without judgment or examination. The dative τῇ σιωπῇ is read as manner, “silently,” though attachment as anger “at the silence” is grammatically conceivable but contextually less natural."},{"source_quote":"πλὴν ἐφ᾽ ὑμῶν αὐτοῦ πεύσομαι","chosen":"Nevertheless, in your presence I will ask him","rationale":"ἐφ᾽ ὑμῶν means “before you” or “in your presence,” while αὐτοῦ is taken as the genitive personal complement of πεύσομαι, supplying “him.” This is syntactically straightforward and identifies Appion as the person questioned. Alternatively, αὐτοῦ may be adverbial, “there” or “on the spot,” with “him” inferred from context."},{"source_quote":"παντοπαθεῖς εἶναι μυθολογούμενοι","chosen":"mythologized as subject to every passion","rationale":"παντοπαθής can describe undergoing every kind of passion, experience, or suffering; the repeated πάθεσιν and the moral context favor “every passion.”"},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν τοῦ ὁμοίου μίμησιν ἐπίτηδες ᾄδονται δημοσία","chosen":"are deliberately sung in public to encourage imitation of such things","rationale":"ἐπίτηδες makes the singing purposeful, and πρὸς with μίμησις expresses its intended movement toward imitation of like conduct."},{"source_quote":"οἱ κατὰ τόπον δείκνυνται τάφοι","chosen":"their tombs are also pointed out in their respective places","rationale":"κατὰ τόπον can mean place by place, locally, or in the respective locations; the rendering preserves the claim that identifiable tombs are shown."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"5.30","text":"The others, having heard these things from me beforehand and longing to learn what came next, joined me, intending to visit Appion. And indeed we found him already bathed at a table that had been made ready; therefore . we went into only a few details concerning the discussion about gods. But he, I think, perceived our purpose and promised that on the following day he would have something to say about gods; and he indicated the same place to us in advance, intending to converse there. With that promise, after expressing our thanks to him, we each departed for home.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προακούσαντες ἐμοῦ","chosen":"having heard these things from me beforehand","rationale":"The prefix in προακούω indicates hearing in advance, and the genitive identifies the narrator as the source."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐπισκεψόμενοι Ἀππίωνα","chosen":"intending to visit Appion","rationale":"ὡς with the future participle expresses the companions’ purpose or intention."},{"source_quote":"λελουμένον αὐτὸν ἤδη κατελαμβάνομεν ἐφ᾽ ἑτοίμῳ τραπέζῃ","chosen":"we found him already bathed at a table that had been made ready","rationale":"λελουμένον depicts Appion as having bathed, while ἐφ᾽ ἑτοίμῳ τραπέζῃ places him at a prepared or ready table."},{"source_quote":"ὀλίγα ἠκριβολογησάμεθα","chosen":"we went into only a few details","rationale":"ἀκριβολογέομαι denotes speaking or discussing with precision; ὀλίγα limits the discussion to a few matters or a small amount."},{"source_quote":"τὸν αὐτὸν προεδήλωσεν ἡμῖν τόπον","chosen":"he indicated the same place to us in advance","rationale":"προδηλόω marks advance indication or notification, and τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον most directly means “the same place.”"},{"source_quote":"σὺν τῇ ὑποσχέσει, χάριν ὁμολογήσαντες αὐτῷ","chosen":"With that promise, after expressing our thanks to him","rationale":"χάριν ὁμολογεῖν means acknowledging or expressing gratitude; σύν retains the promise as the circumstance accompanying their departure."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"διόπερ . ὀλίγα","issue":"The selected image-checked edition prints one isolated dot after διόπερ as a gap marker. The content represented by the gap is unavailable; the translation retains exactly one dot and supplies no restoration. This faithful representation of the selected edition’s printed lacuna does not itself block publication.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
